dek: The streamer's biggest layoffs since 2022 land days before earnings.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Netflix is cutting about *1,000 jobs*, roughly *6%* of its global workforce, The Wall Street Journal first reported.

slides.label: Who's affected
slides.text: Most of the cuts hit *product, technology, legal and HR* teams.

slides.label: The memo
slides.text: Co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters said the mission "requires us to be *disciplined* about where we prioritize our people and resources."

slides.label: Bigger than 2022
slides.text: In 2022, Netflix cut about *450 roles* in two rounds. This round is *more than double* that.

slides.label: The timing
slides.text: The cuts land days before Netflix reports third-quarter earnings on *October 20*.

slides.label: The pressure
slides.text: Shares are down about *20%* this year, and viewing grew only about *2%* in the first half as YouTube competes for screen time.

slides.label: Not alone
slides.text: *Disney and Amazon* have made similar cuts recently. Media and tech are trimming the teams that build the product.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: No title is permanent. Your *skills, network and own projects* are the safety net that travels with you.

question: Is any job in tech truly safe right now? Yes or no.

Netflix is cutting about 1,000 jobs, roughly 6% of its global workforce, its biggest round of layoffs since 2022. The Wall Street Journal first reported the cuts, and co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters confirmed them in a memo to staff.

Most of the roles are in product, technology, legal and HR. The co-CEOs said the company's mission "requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources." The news lands days before Netflix reports earnings on October 20, with shares down about 20% this year and Disney and Amazon making similar cuts.

Is any job in tech truly safe right now? Yes or no.

Netflix is cutting about 1,000 jobs, roughly 6% of its global workforce. It is the company's largest reduction since 2022, when it cut about 450 roles across two rounds.

Most of the affected roles sit in product, technology, legal and HR. In a memo to staff, co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters said the company's mission "requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources."

The timing matters. Netflix reports third-quarter earnings on October 20, shares are down about 20% this year, and first-half engagement grew only about 2% as YouTube competes for viewing time. Disney and Amazon have made similar cuts recently.

For operators across media and tech, the lesson is the same one the last few years keep teaching: your skills, your network and the things you build on your own are what carry forward.

Is any job in tech truly safe right now? Yes or no.
